hypothesis: The gate_rate is only 0.375 and `fix_rounds` is high (4), meaning SEARCH blocks frequently fail to match the shown code. The biggest lever is to make the model copy SEARCH text verbatim from `{CODE}` and, when a knob isn't shown, to refuse to invent it. I'll tighten system.md's HARD RULES into a short, explicit "SEARCH discipline" checklist placed right before OUTPUT PROTOCOL, and add a rule that if the desired knob's code is not in `{CODE}`, the model must pick a shown chunk instead. This should reduce non-matching SEARCH blocks and thus raise first-try gate_rate and lower fix_rounds.

The v1 prompts improved meta_score but gate_rate dropped to 0.0 because the strict "SEARCH must match byte-for-byte" rule combined with short 3-15 line blocks makes the model retype lines from memory and drift. Adding an explicit "copy the whole chunk verbatim then trim" workflow and a self-check checklist in system.md, plus requiring the model to quote the first/last SEARCH line back as verification, should raise first-try gate success without changing cost.
